outcome: Maternal outcome (e.g., pulmonary complications, DIC, renal failure, HELLP, cardiovascular complications, cerebrovascular complications)
Fetal outcome (e.g., live births, still births, NICU admission, neonatal mortality)
cohort: 100 women presenting with eclampsia at a tertiary care center over an 18-month period.
finding: The study concluded that inadequate antenatal care and delay in women seeking help contribute to an increased number of maternal and perinatal complications in eclamptic patients.
mod_finding: Among eclamptic patients, 62% delivered by LSCS, 33% delivered vaginally, and 2% had assisted vaginal deliveries.
gest_age: The cohort included 69 preterm and 31 term deliveries, but specific gestational age ranges were not provided.
